dāmalisutta: [Dāmali+sutta]  CL=8 The Dāmali Sutta: A special discourse given to dispel the misconception of the deva Dāmali, who thought, 'Just as one who has crossed a river and reached the other shore no longer needs to make an effort to swim, an Arahant no longer needs to cultivate or practice the monastic virtues.' Dāmali believed that an Arahant could choose whether or not to make an effort, and if they didn"t want to, they could live comfortably. The deva Dāmali misunderstood, thinking 'An Arahant, even after becoming an Arahant, must continuously cultivate monastic virtues until attaining Parinibbāna.' While other discourses encourage everyone to make intense effort and diligence, this discourse aims to highlight the effectiveness (niyyanika) of the Buddha"s teaching. Therefore, it explains that no further effort is necessary for an Arahant.
